# Code, math and fences {#code}

A code or math span now needs its closer: an unclosed backtick run is text where 0.1 read it as code to the end of the paragraph (C2-I-017). Backticks are the only code fence; `~~~` is text (C2-B-108).

**U-370** <Badge type="danger" text="report" /> <Badge type="warning" text="silent" /> Under C2-B-222, an unclosed code fence whose last line has no line feed at the end of input: ```` ``` ````, `code` and no line feed; also in a quote or a list item
Tool: A line feed after the last line: `<pre><code>code` and a line feed `</code></pre>`. A code value always ends with a line feed, so no source keeps the 0.1 HTML.

::: compare no-render
````text
```
code
````
```text
<pre><code>code
</code></pre> C2-B-222 ends every body line of a code block with a line feed, also the last line of an unclosed fence that the end of input closes without one. 0.1 wrote the value as the input ended, `<pre><code>code</code></pre>`, also in a quote and in a list item. A code value always ends with a line feed in 0.2, so no source gives the 0.1 HTML.
```
:::

**U-396** <Badge type="danger" text="report" /> <Badge type="warning" text="silent" /> An empty unclosed math run at the end of inline content: <code>a $&#96;</code> or <code>$$&#96;&#96;</code>. 0.1 writes an empty math span; 0.2 writes the run as text (C2-I-017).
Tool: Report at the parsed math range.

::: compare no-render
```text
a $`
```
```text
<p>a $`</p> C2-I-017 reads a backtick run with no closer of its length as text, and 0.1 wrote an empty math span. An adjacent closer joins the opener into a wider run, and a separator changes the empty value, so no spelling keeps the empty span. Report the parsed math range, `$` or `$$` with its backticks, at the end of inline content; do not rewrite.
```
:::

**U-439** <Badge type="danger" text="report" /> <Badge type="warning" text="silent" /> An unclosed run whose 0.1 output no 0.2 source spells: an empty code value at the end of inline content, <code>a &#96;</code>; a code, literal-text or math value that starts with a space and a backtick or ends with a backtick and a space, <code>a &#96;&#96; &#96;b</code>; an empty literal-text run that U-440 cannot remove, <code>a !&#96;&#96;</code>.
Tool: Report at the parsed range of the run.

::: compare no-render
```text
a `
```
```text
<p>a `</p> C2-I-017 reads a backtick run with no closer of its length as text, and so is a `!` or `$` glued before it. 0.1 wrote an empty code span for an empty code value; an adjacent closer joins the opener into a wider run, and a separator changes the empty value. A code, literal-text or math value that starts with a space and a backtick, or ends with a backtick and a space, has no spelling either, since C2-I-016 removes that space (C2-W-077). An empty literal-text run that U-440 cannot remove is reported too: 0.1 wrote nothing for it, and the space before it, which 0.2 drops at the end of the content (C2-I-002), or the empty paragraph or heading it filled has no spelling. Report the parsed range of the run and its value; do not rewrite.
```
:::
